title: Quba and the first Friday
hookLine: at Quba he builds a mosque and leads the first Friday prayer on the way into the city (sirah)

cards: For a while, people in Yathrib had walked out to the edge of town every morning to watch the road. That detail is in Bukhari. They'd heard he had left Mecca, so they waited, until the heat drove them back inside.
One day a man up on a high place saw white-clad riders coming out of the shimmer and shouted the news. People ran out to meet them. The travelers didn't go straight into the city.
They stopped first at Quba, a village on its outskirts. Today: al-jumu'ah.

teach.b: In Bukhari's account, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, stays some nights at Quba with the clan of Banu Amr ibn Awf, and lays the foundation of a mosque.

Bukhari connects it to a verse in surah nine about a place of worship founded on devotion to Allah from its first day, with people in it who love to purify themselves. Muslims still pray at Quba today.
Before a house for himself in the city, he builds a place to pray. Then he rides on toward the town.
Ibn Ishaq says a Friday came while he was on the way, among the clan of Banu Salim ibn Awf, and he led the Friday prayer there, in a valley, with the people around him, the first he led in Medina.
Some reports say the believers of Yathrib had already been gathering on Fridays before he came, so the careful way to say it is: his first Friday among them.

Here's how the Qur'an names the day, in surah sixty-two, in Pickthall's words: "When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading."
The day of congregation. In Arabic, al-jumu'ah, the gathering. That's what this week has been walking toward.
People slipping out of Mecca one by one, two men in a cave, a belt torn in half, a hunter turned back, a woman's thin goat.
And near the end of the road, before he has even entered the city, they gather, in a valley, on a Friday, and pray together.

how: Muslims gather each Friday at midday for Jumu'ah, a congregational prayer with a sermon (khutbah); visitors to Medina also pray at the mosque of Quba.

games.q: you've just arrived after a dangerous journey, at the edge of the city that has invited you. what do you build first?
games.why: at Quba, Bukhari says, he founded a mosque, and on the road into the city he led a Friday prayer.

practice: If you're Muslim, picture this week's Jumu'ah: the time, the place, and what trading you'll leave for an hour.

If you're not, bring to mind a gathering you belong to, or used to, and either way, picture the people you'd be standing beside and name a few of them quietly. If you pray, you can ask Allah to bless the gathering.

wordCard.voice: Quba, the village on Yathrib's edge, where the Prophet founded a mosque first, before he had even built a house for himself. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'the gathering', the name of Friday and of the Friday prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: the first Friday. Scattered roads, and then one gathering. Day seven hundred seventy, done.
